In this blog, I will use Python to compare the body mass across three penguins species from `palmerpenguins` dataset.

## Setup

- Import relevant packages.

```{python}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
```

## Loading and cleaning the data

- Loading the data and drop rows with missing values for further analysis.

```{python}
penguins = load_penguins()
penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=["body_mass_g"])
penguins_clean.head(5)
```

## Summary by species

- Calculate the number of penguins and their average body mass for each species.

```{python}
mass_summary = (
    penguins_clean
    .groupby("species")["body_mass_g"]
    .agg(count="count", avg_mass_g="mean")
    .round(2)
    .reset_index()
)
mass_summary
```

## Visualizing body mass

- @fig-penguin-mass visualize how body mass is spread out within each species.
- **Findings**: Gentoo penguins are the heaviest of the three species.
Adelie and Chinstrap penguins have similar average body mass.

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass
#| fig-cap: "Body mass of penguins by species"
alt.Chart(penguins_clean).mark_boxplot(size=50).encode(
    x=alt.X("species:N", title="Species"),
    y=alt.Y("body_mass_g:Q", title="Body mass (g)"),
    color=alt.Color("species:N", legend=None)
).properties(
    width=400,
    height=260
)
```
